articles.title: Auditing Climate Risk: Scope 1, 2 and 3 Emissions under IFRS S2
articles.summary: Dawgen Global provides internal-audit procedures for IFRS S2 across climate governance, scenario analysis, Scope 1, 2 and 3 emissions, and climate metrics and targets. It explains evidence and control checks for emissions boundaries, factors, data quality and target credibility, with examples for Caribbean physical and transition risks.

articles.title: Bridging the Climate Finance Gap: Reaching US$1.3 Trillion Annually by 2035
articles.summary: Deloitte examines the mix of public, private, multilateral, carbon-market and philanthropic finance that could support emerging markets and developing economies. It finds that reaching the aspirational US$1.3 trillion annual target by 2035 depends on stronger enabling conditions and greater capital mobilisation.

articles.title: Natural Catastrophe and Weather Resiliency: National and State Insurance Efforts
articles.summary: Deloitte surveys US national and state initiatives that connect catastrophe mitigation, insurance regulation, risk modelling, resilience grants and premium incentives. The paper frames pre-disaster investment and stronger property standards as tools for reducing losses and supporting insurance affordability.

articles.title: Preparing for Climate-Related Disclosure in the Insurance Sector
articles.summary: Deloitte outlines seven considerations for insurers preparing for climate-related disclosure, including governance, stakeholder skills, data controls, risk identification and assurance readiness. The article links the proposed SEC framework to TCFD and the GHG Protocol and stresses integration with insurers' existing financial and risk-control processes.

articles.title: Climate Risks Shift from an Insurance Challenge to a Financial Stability Concern
articles.summary: The article describes physical climate risk as an issue that can move beyond insurance balance sheets into broader financial stability. It highlights rising catastrophe losses, protection gaps and the importance of insurance availability to financing and economic resilience.

articles.title: EIOPA and ESM Staff Propose a European Mechanism for Outsized Natural Catastrophes
articles.summary: EIOPA and European Stability Mechanism staff propose a European mechanism to complement national schemes and private insurance when exceptionally large natural catastrophes exceed available capacity. The proposal aims to improve risk sharing, preserve fiscal and financial stability, and narrow Europe's catastrophe protection gap.

articles.title: Insurance Protection Gaps in a Changing Climate
articles.summary: EIOPA explains why climate-driven natural catastrophes are widening the gap between economic and insured losses in Europe. It discusses household risk perception, affordability and market capacity alongside public-private approaches that could sustain coverage and strengthen resilience.

articles.title: Applying the Targeted IFRS S2 Amendments on Greenhouse Gas Emissions
articles.summary: EY explains the targeted IFRS S2 amendments affecting greenhouse-gas disclosures, including relief concerning Scope 3 Category 15 financed emissions for financial institutions. The paper describes the measurement and disclosure implications for entities applying the amended standard.

articles.title: ISSB Climate-Related Disclosure Checklist
articles.summary: EY provides a structured checklist for assessing climate-related disclosures against IFRS S2 and related ISSB requirements. It is designed as an implementation and completeness aid for preparers and reviewers, including the amended greenhouse-gas provisions.

articles.title: Billion Dollar Disasters: Why Your Insurance Is Getting More Expensive
articles.summary: Forbes links the rising cost of insurance to climate impacts, aging infrastructure and a 2025 natural-catastrophe loss baseline dominated by wildfires, severe convective storms and floods. It describes higher premiums, deductibles and exclusions alongside greater use of forward-looking models, parametric insurance and resilience investment.

articles.title: Task Force on Climate-related Financial Disclosures
articles.summary: TCFD developed a framework for organisations to disclose climate-related risks and opportunities through governance, strategy, risk management, and metrics and targets. The task force disbanded after its 2023 status report, and the Financial Stability Board asked the IFRS Foundation to monitor companies' climate-related disclosures.

articles.title: Swiss Re Sees Natural-Catastrophe Claims Rising in 2026
articles.summary: The article cites Swiss Re's estimate that insured natural-catastrophe losses could rise to about US$148 billion in 2026, with a severe scenario reaching US$320 billion. Swiss Re characterises the lower 2025 outcome as favourable variability rather than an easing of underlying catastrophe risk.

articles.title: Measuring Climate Change from an Actuarial Perspective
articles.summary: The article surveys actuarial applications of composite climate indices, including measures derived from weather and climate extremes. It considers how such indices can support analysis of insurance exposure, balance-sheet effects and business sustainability.

articles.title: Financial Stability Implications of Natural-Catastrophe Insurance Protection Gaps
articles.summary: The IAIS examines how gaps between catastrophe losses and insurance coverage can amplify economic disruption and create financial-stability concerns. It positions insurance availability, risk reduction and coordinated public-private action as important elements of resilience.

articles.title: IAIS Climate-Risk Supervisory Work
articles.summary: The IAIS climate-risk topic page brings together its supervisory priorities, market monitoring, guidance and capacity-building work for the insurance sector. It covers the management of physical, transition and liability risks and connects climate issues with prudential supervision and financial stability.

articles.title: IAIS Holistic Framework for Systemic Risk in the Insurance Sector
articles.summary: The IAIS Holistic Framework sets out a sector-wide approach to assessing and mitigating systemic risk in insurance. It combines supervisory policy measures, global monitoring and implementation assessment rather than relying only on a fixed list of systemically important insurers.

articles.title: Carbon Capture, Utilisation and Storage
articles.summary: The IEA describes carbon capture, utilisation and storage as a group of technologies for capturing carbon dioxide from industrial and energy sources, transporting it and either using it or storing it permanently. The page tracks deployment and the technology's role in emissions-reduction pathways.

articles.title: Unlocking the Potential of Bioenergy with Carbon Capture and Utilisation or Storage
articles.summary: The IEA describes BECCUS as capturing carbon dioxide from biomass-based energy and either storing it or using it in products, thereby combining renewable-energy production with atmospheric carbon removal. The project analyses supply-chain carbon accounting and obstacles to sustainable deployment, including policy frameworks, business models and carbon-transport infrastructure.

articles.title: Integrating Solar and Wind: Global Experience and Emerging Challenges
articles.summary: The IEA reports that solar and wind capacity more than doubled between 2018 and 2023, making timely integration important for 2030 decarbonisation goals. Its stocktake of 50 power systems identifies integration measures and highlights increasingly complex stability, flexibility, planning and financing challenges at high levels of variable renewable penetration.

articles.title: Renewables and Low-Emissions Fuels
articles.summary: The IEA's current page groups renewable power and low-emissions energy technologies including bioenergy, hydrogen, nuclear power and carbon capture. It presents technology indicators and partnerships used to track progress in the energy transition.

articles.title: Tracking the Impact of Fossil-Fuel Subsidies
articles.summary: The IEA tracks the scale and characteristics of fossil-fuel consumption subsidies and explains how they distort energy prices, fiscal balances and incentives for cleaner energy. The page also provides country and fuel-level data using the IEA's price-gap methodology.

articles.title: From Commitment to Action: Six Practical Steps for Government Climate Disclosure
articles.summary: IFAC presents a six-step implementation path for governments developing climate-related disclosures. It frames public-sector disclosure as a process requiring institutional ownership, suitable standards, reliable data, professional capacity and credible publication.

articles.title: Exposure Draft of Proposed Amendments to the SASB Standards
articles.summary: The ISSB paper presents an exposure draft of proposed amendments to the SASB Standards, including climate-related industry content used with IFRS S2 guidance. It documents the proposed text and the board's due-process basis for consultation and ratification.

articles.title: Biogenic Emissions: Applying IFRS S2
articles.summary: This ISSB implementation paper examines how IFRS S2 greenhouse-gas requirements apply to biogenic emissions. It considers the treatment and presentation of those emissions within Scope 2 and Scope 3 disclosures and the interaction with referenced measurement methods.

articles.title: IFRS Sustainability Standards Navigator
articles.summary: The IFRS Sustainability Standards Navigator is the Foundation's structured access point for IFRS S1, IFRS S2 and related requirements and implementation materials. It helps users navigate authoritative sustainability-disclosure content by standard and topic.

articles.title: IFRS Foundation Updates and Podcasts
articles.summary: This IFRS Foundation page is the central chronological index for IASB and ISSB board updates and accompanying podcasts. It directs users to summaries of decisions and work-plan developments, including sustainability and climate-disclosure matters.

articles.title: International Sustainability Standards Board
articles.summary: The IFRS Foundation page describes the ISSB and provides access to its membership, meetings, projects and standard-setting work. The board develops investor-focused sustainability-disclosure standards, including the climate requirements in IFRS S2.

articles.title: IFRS S2 Climate-Related Disclosures
articles.summary: IFRS S2 requires entities to disclose decision-useful information about climate-related risks and opportunities that could affect cash flows, access to finance or cost of capital. Its core content covers governance, strategy, risk management, and metrics and targets.

articles.title: March 2026 ISSB Update and Podcast
articles.summary: The IFRS Foundation publishes the ISSB's March 2026 board update and podcast and directs users to decisions and materials from that month's meetings. The material covers ongoing sustainability-standard setting and implementation work, including climate-related disclosure.

articles.title: Climate Resilience and Scenario Analysis Requirements in IFRS S2
articles.summary: The IFRS Foundation webcast explains the IFRS S2 requirement to disclose an assessment of climate resilience informed by climate-related scenario analysis. It also describes proportionality mechanisms that let an entity choose an approach commensurate with its circumstances.

articles.title: Powering Moldova's Green Future through Skills Training
articles.summary: The ILO profiles a young woman in Moldova who turns vocational skills training into a career in renewable energy. The project, funded by Liechtenstein and Austria, supports modernised vocational education and prepares workers for Moldova's green transition.

articles.title: A Young Indonesian Looks Beyond Coal toward a Greener South Sumatra
articles.summary: The ILO describes an initiative that encourages a university student in South Sumatra to consider a future beyond the province's coal economy. The story illustrates youth participation, green skills and the employment dimension of a just transition.

articles.title: High Temperatures Linked to Increased Worker Mortality in Colombia
articles.summary: An ILO working paper finds that high temperatures are associated with greater mortality risk among workers in Colombia. Agricultural workers, assemblers, and health and teaching professionals are among the occupational groups identified as facing elevated exposure.

articles.title: Climate Risks: The Role of Financial Regulators and Supervisors
articles.summary: The IMF technical note sets out how financial regulators and supervisors can address climate-related risks within their mandates. It covers governance, risk assessment, scenario analysis and supervisory tools for integrating climate considerations into prudential oversight.

articles.title: Parametric Insurance Market Size and Growth Forecast
articles.summary: The commercial market study describes parametric insurance and forecasts growth across natural-catastrophe, agriculture and other trigger-based applications. It segments the market by product, peril, customer and geography and attributes demand to faster payouts and expanding climate exposure.

articles.title: Climate Risk Disclosure Survey
articles.summary: The California Department of Insurance page provides instructions and materials for insurers subject to the NAIC Climate Risk Disclosure Survey. It identifies the applicable reporting cycle, filing process and compliance dates for participating insurance companies.

articles.title: Natural-Disaster Insured Losses Exceed US$100 Billion for a Second Year
articles.summary: The article relays Munich Re's finding that global insured losses from natural disasters exceeded US$100 billion for a second consecutive year. It underscores that severe loss totals can persist even without a major US hurricane landfall, reflecting a broad catastrophe-loss burden.

articles.title: Fewer Storms Expected in 2026, but Insurers Still Face Losses
articles.summary: The article contrasts a below-average Atlantic hurricane-season outlook with the continuing potential for a single landfalling storm to cause severe insured losses. It cautions insurers against treating seasonal storm counts as a substitute for exposure-based catastrophe pricing and reserving.

articles.title: Natural-Catastrophe Risks in 2026: Uncertainty amid Escalating Loss Trends
articles.summary: The article presents HDI Global's view that natural-catastrophe losses are likely to remain above average while individual-event outcomes stay highly volatile. It stresses the interaction of hazard, exposure and vulnerability and the need for disciplined risk management despite uncertain annual results.

articles.title: EIOPA Makes a Splash in the EU NatCat Risk Pool Debate
articles.summary: InsuranceERM's archive says EIOPA and the European Stability Mechanism published proposals for a European natural-catastrophe risk pool. Industry views are divided and policymakers have not decided the way forward, making implementation challenging.

articles.title: The Talent Gap in Insurance Has Become a Strategic Risk
articles.summary: InsuranceERM's archive says the insurance industry's talent gap is longstanding but is beginning to affect revenue and warrants greater attention. The excerpt attributes this assessment to Louisa Blain, Aon's head of insurance for human capital.

articles.title: Canadian Insurers Push Owners to Fortify Homes against Climate Risks
articles.summary: Canadian property and casualty insurers are encouraging flood- and wildfire-resilient home improvements as climate-related claims and premiums rise. The article describes insurer investment in mitigation, risk modelling and customer incentives and calls for stronger building codes and limits on construction in high-risk areas.

articles.title: Business Interruption Insurance Must Catch Up with Climate Volatility
articles.summary: The viewpoint argues that conventional business-interruption policies often leave small and medium-sized businesses exposed when extreme weather forces closures without producing covered physical damage. It calls for clearer terms and product innovation suited to increasingly volatile climate hazards.

articles.title: Wildfires, Storms, Floods Account for Record 92% of Global Insured Losses: Swiss Re
articles.summary: Insurance Journal reports that secondary perils generated a record 92% of the US$107 billion in global insured natural-catastrophe losses in 2025, led by wildfires, severe convective storms and floods. Swiss Re projects US$148 billion of 2026 losses at the long-term trend and about US$320 billion in its modelled peak-loss scenario.

articles.title: Worsening Ocean Heatwaves Are Supercharging Hurricane Damage
articles.summary: The article covers research linking marine heatwaves with faster intensification and greater damage from landfalling tropical cyclones. It notes that warmer ocean conditions are increasingly occurring near coastlines, creating a material variable for catastrophe modelling and coastal insurance exposure.

articles.title: Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change
articles.summary: The IPCC is the United Nations body for assessing climate-change science. Its site provides access to assessment cycles, working groups, special and methodology publications, data and current activities, including the Seventh Assessment Report programme.

articles.title: IPCC Authors Advance the 2027 CDR and CCUS Methodology Draft
articles.summary: More than 120 IPCC authors met in Mexico City from 11 to 14 August 2026 to advance the first-order draft of the 2027 methodology on carbon dioxide removal and carbon capture, utilisation and storage. The Task Force on National Greenhouse Gas Inventories is preparing the document for publication in 2027.

articles.title: IPCC Opens Review of the 2027 Short-Lived Climate Forcers Methodology
articles.summary: The IPCC opened registration for expert reviewers of the second-order draft of its 2027 methodology for inventories of short-lived climate forcers. The guidance will address estimation and disclosure of national annual anthropogenic emissions, including substances such as nitrogen oxides and carbon monoxide.

articles.title: IPCC Workshops on Diverse Knowledge Systems and Methods of Assessment
articles.summary: The event page covers IPCC workshops on engaging diverse knowledge systems and on methods of assessment. The activities concern how climate assessments gather, evaluate and combine evidence from different forms of knowledge.

articles.title: Second Lead Author Meeting for the 2027 CDR and CCUS Methodology
articles.summary: The IPCC convened more than 120 authors in Mexico City from 11 to 14 August 2026 for the second lead-author meeting on its carbon-removal and CCUS methodology. Participants worked to develop and consolidate the first-order draft for the Task Force on National Greenhouse Gas Inventories.

articles.title: Third Lead Author Meeting for the Special Report on Climate Change and Cities
articles.summary: More than 100 scientists from 56 countries met in Oslo in January 2026 to advance the second-order draft of the IPCC Special Report on Climate Change and Cities. The planned 2027 assessment covers urban climate impacts and risks as well as adaptation and mitigation options.

articles.title: 2027 IPCC Methodology for Carbon Dioxide Removal and CCUS Inventories
articles.summary: The IPCC methodology project will provide additional guidance for national greenhouse-gas inventories covering carbon dioxide removal and carbon capture, utilisation and storage. Its agreed structure follows the 2006 IPCC Guidelines, with an overview and six volumes designed for use by inventory compilers.

articles.title: ISO 14091:2021 — Adaptation to Climate Change: Guidelines on Vulnerability, Impacts and Risk Assessment
articles.summary: ISO 14091 gives guidelines for assessing risks from the potential impacts of climate change, understanding vulnerability, and developing sound assessments of present and future risks. These assessments support adaptation planning, implementation, monitoring and evaluation for organisations of any size or type.

articles.title: Parametric Insurance: Key Trends and Mapfre's Vision
articles.summary: Mapfre explains how objective thresholds such as rainfall, wind speed or earthquake magnitude can trigger fast parametric payouts without a conventional on-site loss assessment. It links growth in these products to climate hazards, high-resolution and satellite data, predictive analytics and efforts to expand protection in underinsured markets.
